items.description: A working preview of Section shell.

items.name: sidebar-layout
items.title: Sidebar layout
items.description: A sidebar beside content that wraps above it by itself when the content gets too narrow, with no breakpoints.
items.docs: sidebar and children are the two columns; side is start or end, and the DOM follows what people see on the wide layout, so a start sidebar comes first and an end sidebar last. sidebarWidth is the width the sidebar prefers (18rem) and contentMin the least share of the row the content may have (60%): when the content would fall below it, the sidebar wraps onto its own line and fills it. The switch reads the space the layout has, not the viewport, so it works in a dialog, a sheet or a narrow card; it happens at (sidebarWidth + gap) / (1 - contentMin). gap is none, sm, md or lg, or any length. sticky pins the sidebar while the content scrolls (true for 1rem from the top, or a length such as 5rem to clear a header); it only pins while the two are side by side, and the sidebar scrolls inside itself when it is taller than the screen. Pinning makes the layout a size container, so it has to fill its parent.

items.name: sidebar-layout-demo
items.title: Sidebar layout demo
items.description: A working preview of Sidebar layout.

items.name: reading-column
items.title: Reading column
items.description: A comfortable reading measure where figures, tables and code can break out wider, or all the way to the edge.
items.docs: Children sit in the text column, measure wide (50 by default). measure is in ch, the width of a zero in the column's font, and not a count of characters: a zero is wider than the average letter, so 50ch holds about 60 to 75 characters on a line, depending on the font. ReadingColumn.Wide takes the width of the page content (wideWidth, 72rem) and ReadingColumn.Full runs edge to edge, for pictures, tables, code and pull quotes. Every track is sized from the grid itself and not from viewport units, so a wide or full child never causes sideways scroll, and on a phone everything collapses into one column with gutters (the fluid gutters of Container). gap is the space between blocks (sm, md, lg or any length) and as renders a div, article, main or section. Put the column in a parent that is as wide as the page, so Full can reach the edges.

items.title: Reading column demo
items.description: A working preview of Reading column.

items.name: full-bleed-band
items.title: Full-bleed band
items.description: A section background that runs edge to edge while its content stays on the page column, with no horizontal scrollbar.
items.docs: A FullBleedBand breaks out of its column to the full width of the nearest FullBleedBand.Root, which you put around the page once. The break-out is measured from that wrapper (a container query unit) and not from 100vw, so a classic vertical scrollbar never adds a stray horizontal one, and the wrapper clips what could overshoot. The band must sit in a column that is centred in the wrapper, such as a Container. tone is default, muted or inverted: an inverted band swaps the semantic tokens for its children (background, foreground, muted, border, primary and the rest), so text, borders and buttons stay readable in both themes. size is the vertical padding (none, sm, md, lg, xl), bordered draws a line along the top, the bottom or both, contentWidth takes the sizes of Container so the content lines up with the page, and as renders a section, aside, header, footer or nav.

items.name: inset-panel
items.title: Inset panel
items.description: A padded panel whose images, tables and code can reach its edges: the inset cancels the padding and rounds with the corners.
items.docs: padding is sm (16px), md (24px) or lg (32px), and is kept in one CSS variable, --inset-panel-padding. InsetPanel.Inset cancels it on the sides you choose: x (the default), y, all, top, bottom, start or end. top and bottom also reach the sides next to them, so a picture runs across the whole top; start and end also reach the top and bottom. An inset rounds only the corners that touch the panel's edge, with the panel's own radius less its 1px border, so no sliver of background shows. Content wider than the panel, such as a table, scrolls inside the inset and never widens the panel; where scrollbars are classic the inset shows a thin, soft one.

items.name: aligned-card-grid
items.title: Aligned card grid
items.description: Cards that line up inside: every card is a subgrid, so titles, bodies and footers share rows and the buttons sit on one baseline.
items.docs: Build a grid with AlignedCardGrid and put AlignedCardGrid.Card in it: each card is a subgrid with one row for every part you list in rows (media, title, body and footer by default), so the parts of cards side by side share their rows. Write the parts of a card in the order of rows: Media (with an optional ratio such as 4/3; the picture runs to the edge of the card), Title (an h3, or the level you pass with as), Body and Footer, or Part with a name for a row of your own (rows={["title", "body", "price", "features", "footer"]} and <AlignedCardGrid.Part name="price">). A card may leave a part out and its neighbours keep their rows; list only the rows that exist, so a row nobody uses takes no room. The card itself has 20px of room under its last part, so a card without a footer still ends clear of its text (pass pb-0 to a card whose last part is a picture). minCardWidth is the narrowest a card may get (16rem by default) and the grid fits as many columns as the width allows, stretching the cards when a row is short; gap is sm, md, lg or any length. Where subgrid is missing the cards are flex columns of equal height with the footer pushed to the bottom. The cards use the Card surface. For a list, give the grid role="list" and each card role="listitem".

items.name: collapsing-columns
items.title: Collapsing columns
items.description: Equal columns that stack all at once when their own container gets narrow, with no awkward two-plus-one in between.
items.docs: The cells are the children, two to five of them. threshold is the width of the container, any CSS length, below which they stack in one step (40rem by default). It is measured on the content width of this element, never on the window, so the same component is a row on a wide page and a column in a sidebar or a dialog, with no media query and no script. gap is none, sm, md, lg or a length, and applies between the columns and between the rows once stacked; align is start, center, end or stretch (the default: equal heights); as is div, section, ul or ol, with li cells for a list. The cells share the width evenly and may shrink to nothing, so a long word breaks instead of widening its cell. The source order is the stacked order.

items.title: Collapsing columns demo
items.description: A working preview of Collapsing columns.

items.name: leader-list
items.title: Leader list
items.description: Rows with a dotted leader between the name and the value, for menus, schedules, receipts and tables of contents.
items.docs: items are the rows: a label, a value and an optional detail (a quieter line under the label), with an id when two labels could be the same. leader is dots (the default), dashes or line; size is sm, md or lg. as="ul" (the default) renders a list, as="dl" renders term and description pairs. The label and the value can be any node, so a total can be bold and a chapter number muted. The leader is CSS: it starts a little after the last word of the label and stops before the value, a long label wraps onto a second line while the leader and the value stay on its last line, and the value never wraps and uses tabular figures. The leader is hidden from assistive technology, and it follows the writing direction, so it works right to left.

items.description: A working preview of Leader list.

items.name: inline-list
items.title: Inline list
items.description: Meta lines whose separators never dangle: a byline wraps without a dot at the start or end of a line.
items.docs: The items are the children, and anything empty (null, false) is skipped, so a conditional item leaves no stray separator. separator is dot (the default), slash, pipe or none; gap is sm, md, lg or a length, measured in the type size; align is start, center or end; size is xs, sm or md; as is div (plain text) or ul (a list, whose separators are hidden from assistive technology). Each item stays on one line unless you pass nowrap={false}, so a break only ever happens between items. The separator is a shape painted behind the space between two items, which the browser removes where a line breaks, so one never starts a line or ends one, in any alignment, and there is no script.

items.title: Inline list demo
items.description: A working preview of Inline list.

items.name: holy-grail-layout
items.title: Holy grail layout
items.description: The classic page skeleton: header, navigation, main, aside and footer, with the footer pinned to the bottom of short pages.
items.docs: children is main; header, nav, aside and footer are optional and render as header, nav (named by navLabel), aside (named by asideLabel) and footer. In a layout 64rem wide the three columns stand side by side (navWidth and asideWidth, 14rem and 15rem by default); from 48rem the aside drops under main; below that the navigation is a block above everything and the aside comes last, in one column. The footer sits at the bottom of a page shorter than the screen: height is the screen (100dvh by default; give it a length to fill a box). stickyHeader pins the header, stickyColumns pins the navigation and the aside under it while main scrolls (they scroll inside themselves when taller than the screen, and they only pin where they stand beside main); headerHeight is the height of the header, 3.5rem by default. A skip link comes first and points at main (mainId, skipLabel, or false to leave it out). mainAs is main (the default) or div: a page has one main landmark, so a second layout on the page, a preview or a dialog uses div. classNames reaches each part. The layout is a size container, so it answers to its own width and works in a dialog or a preview.

items.title: Holy grail layout demo
items.description: A working preview of Holy grail layout.

items.name: split-screen
items.title: Split screen
items.description: Two full-height halves, one for the task and one for a brand panel or picture, which folds away on a phone.
items.docs: children is the task and becomes the main landmark; media is the other half. mediaSide is start or end (default end), ratio is 1:1 or 3:2, which gives the task three parts and the media two. mediaOnMobile is what the media does below 48rem of width: hidden (the default), banner (a short strip above the task) or top (a taller block above it), so the form is never pushed below the fold. stickyMedia (on by default) pins the media to the screen while a long task scrolls past; off, the media grows as tall as the task. mediaLabel makes the media a labelled complementary region; without it the media is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. height is the height of one screen, 100dvh by default; give it a length to fill a box. mediaClassName and taskClassName reach the halves. mainAs is main (the default) or div, for a second layout on one page, a preview or a dialog, because a page has one main landmark. In the document the task comes first, whichever side the picture is on.

items.name: split-screen-demo
items.title: Split screen demo
items.description: A working preview of Split screen.

items.name: screen-frame
items.title: Screen frame
items.description: A frame that fills the visible screen: header and footer stay put, the middle scrolls, and it copes with address bars, notches and keyboards.
items.docs: header and footer render as header and footer landmarks and stay put; children is the middle, the one part that scrolls, and you put main there. scroll="body" (the default) makes the middle one scrolling area; scroll="none" makes it a row for ScreenFrame.Pane, each of which scrolls on its own (as is div, section, aside or nav). The frame is as tall as the dynamic viewport (h-dvh), so the browser bar never hides the footer; give it a height of your own (h-full, h-[34rem]) to fill a box. The safe-area insets are padding on the frame, and the browser reports them when the viewport meta tag has viewport-fit=cover. keyboardAware (on by default) lifts the footer above the on-screen keyboard, measured through the visual viewport and ignoring pinch zoom; keyboardInset replaces the measurement when you know the height. The body has its overscroll contained; bodyClassName, headerClassName and footerClassName reach each part.

items.name: screen-frame-demo
items.title: Screen frame demo
items.description: A working preview of Screen frame.

items.name: status-bar
items.title: Status bar
items.description: The thin strip at the foot of an editor or tool: facts on both sides, each a button or plain text, the least important dropping out when space runs out.
items.docs: start and end are arrays of segments, most important first: an id, a label, an optional icon (iconOnly shows it alone), onSelect (the segment becomes a button), tooltip, ariaLabel for a fuller name, live (a change of its label is announced politely, with announcement for a longer sentence), priority and disabled. A segment without onSelect is plain text. separators draws a hairline between neighbours, as is div (a labelled region) or footer, and label names the region. The bar measures the natural width of every segment and keeps the most important ones that fit, by priority and then by position, the first of each side first: a segment leaves whole and returns when there is room again, and one that has left is inert, so Tab never reaches it. It is 28px high and uses only the border and muted tokens.

items.name: status-bar-demo
items.title: Status bar demo
items.description: A working preview of Status bar.

items.name: collapsible-panes
items.title: Collapsible panes
items.description: Stacked panes that share the height: open ones split the space and scroll on their own, closed ones fold to a header.
items.docs: panes is the list: an id, a title, an optional count and actions (buttons for the header, shown while the pane is open) and the content. openIds and onOpenIdsChange control which are open (defaultOpenIds when the component keeps the state); multiple (on by default) lets several share the height, off opens one at a time. The open panes divide the height of the component, so give it a height; each content scrolls inside its pane, and minPaneHeight (120px) is the least height an open pane gets. When there is not room for every open pane at that height, the ones that cannot meet it fold, the last first and never the one a person just opened, and they open again when there is room. Headers are buttons in headings (headingLevel, 3 by default) with aria-expanded and aria-controls; ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home and End move between them. The content of an open pane takes focus, so the keyboard can scroll it; the content of a folded pane stays mounted and inert, so it keeps its scroll position and its state.

items.name: collapsible-panes-demo
items.title: Collapsible panes demo
items.description: A working preview of Collapsible panes.

items.name: chrome-offsets
items.title: Chrome offsets
items.description: Measures your fixed header and bottom bar and publishes their heights as CSS variables for sticky things to use.
items.docs: Wrap the page in ChromeOffsets and wrap each fixed bar in a ChromeOffsets.Top, Bottom, Start or End. A part measures what it holds, which is the fixed bar inside it; or give the part the classes that fix it (and as, to make it a header, nav, footer or aside) and let it be the bar. The provider writes --chrome-top, --chrome-bottom, --chrome-start and --chrome-end on its own element as pixel lengths, kept current with a ResizeObserver on every bar, so calc(var(--chrome-top) + 1rem) works for a sticky sidebar, a scroll margin, an anchored heading or the padding of the page. Bars on one edge add up, and an edge whose bars have all gone is zero. defaults (top, bottom, start, end in pixels) are what the variables are on the server and without JavaScript: set them to the sizes at rest. useChromeOffsets() returns the same four sizes as numbers, inside the provider. FloatingStack reads the variables when you pass respectChrome.

items.name: chrome-offsets-demo
items.title: Chrome offsets demo
items.description: A working preview of Chrome offsets.

items.name: floating-stack
items.title: Floating stack
items.description: A corner for floating widgets that do not collide: back to top, a chat launcher and a feedback tab stack with safe gaps.
items.docs: The children are your widgets, the first one nearest the corner. corner is bottom-end (the default), bottom-start, top-end or top-start; end and start follow the writing direction. gap is sm, md, lg or a length; offset is the distance from the edges in pixels or any CSS length, 20 by default, with the safe-area insets added. The stack ignores pointer events and only its children receive them, it hides in print, and the document order equals the visual order from the corner, so Tab reaches the widget in the corner first. respectChrome lifts a bottom stack above a fixed bottom bar or the on-screen keyboard, whichever reaches higher (the keyboard covers the bar and the home indicator, so the two are never added up), and drops a top stack under a fixed header: it reads --chrome-bottom and --chrome-top, which ChromeOffsets publishes, and measures the keyboard through the visual viewport (keyboardInset replaces the measurement). label names the group for assistive technology.

items.name: floating-stack-demo
items.title: Floating stack demo
items.description: A working preview of Floating stack.

items.name: hairline-grid
items.title: Hairline grid
items.description: Cells divided by single hairlines: no doubled rules, no line on the outer edge, and a short last row that never leaves a grey slot or a stray line.
items.docs: Put HairlineGridCell elements in a HairlineGrid. columns is a number or a map per breakpoint ({ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 4 }, a missing breakpoint keeps the one before it); minCell sets the narrowest a cell may get and lets the width decide the number of columns. bordered adds a rounded frame, padding (none, sm, md, lg) is the padding of every cell, and as makes the grid a ul or ol, with as="li" on the cells. A cell with asChild around a link or a button gets a hover tint and an inset focus ring that stay inside its own box. The cells are painted in --hg-cell, which is the page background unless you set it on the grid.

items.title: Hairline grid demo
items.description: A working preview of Hairline grid.

items.name: bento-layout
items.title: Bento layout
items.description: Mixed-size tiles from a named pattern: pick one, pass the tiles as children, and every span is worked out, including a list that keeps growing.
items.docs: pattern is feature-left, feature-top, mosaic, split or quartet. The children fill the pattern in order, so put the most important one first: it gets the largest cell. A list longer than one run continues in a second run, and a last run that is cut short shares one row instead of leaving holes. The layout reads its own width: twelve columns when it is wide, two on a tablet and one on a phone, with the first tile still first. gap is sm, md or lg and rowHeight is sm, md or lg. Each child is wrapped in a plain tile with one radius and the height of its cell; give the child a surface of its own.

items.name: bento-layout-demo
items.title: Bento layout demo
items.description: A working preview of Bento layout.

items.name: progressive-image
items.title: Progressive image
items.description: An image that arrives gracefully: a blurred placeholder in the right shape, a fade to the sharp picture, and a Retry button if it fails.
items.docs: Give it src and alt, and either ratio or the file's width and height, so the space is reserved before anything loads. blurDataURL (a tiny picture) or placeholderColor paints under the image until it has decoded; an image that was already there, from the cache or the server's HTML, shows without the fade. If it fails to load you get a quiet placeholder with the alt text and Retry; onRetry lets you swap the address. priority loads at once with a high fetch priority, fit is cover or contain, and src may be left out while the address is still unknown. With asChild it wraps your own element, such as a next/image with fill, and gives it the same behaviour.

items.name: progressive-image-demo
items.title: Progressive image demo
items.description: A working preview of Progressive image.

items.name: thumbnail-strip
items.title: Thumbnail strip
items.description: A row or column of small previews that chooses the big picture: arrow-key selection, the active one ringed and scrolled into view, and fading edges.
items.docs: items are { id, src, alt, kind, duration }; value, defaultValue and onChange(id, item, index) choose the one shown in the large picture. The strip is one tab stop: the arrow keys move and choose, Home and End jump, and every preview is a button with aria-current. orientation is horizontal or vertical (give a vertical strip a height), size is sm, md or lg, and ratio is the shape of a preview. A video shows a play badge and its length. When there is more than fits it scrolls natively, and the fade at an edge grows with the scroll as more of the strip lies beyond it.

items.name: thumbnail-strip-demo
items.title: Thumbnail strip demo
items.description: A working preview of Thumbnail strip.

items.name: zoomable-image
items.title: Zoomable image
items.description: An image you can zoom in place: click or tap for 2x, wheel or pinch for more, drag to pan, and buttons and keys for everyone else.
items.docs: Click or tap toggles 2x around the point you hit, Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel and a pinch zoom up to maxZoom (4 by default), and a drag pans without the edge of the picture ever showing. Zoom in, Zoom out and a Reset button that shows the level sit in the corner; with the picture focused, + - and 0 zoom and the arrow keys move it. highResSrc is a sharper file, loaded the first time the zoom passes 1.5. A new src starts over at 100% and asks for its own sharper file only when it is looked at closely, so the picture can follow a thumbnail strip. onZoomChange gets the zoom, the step back to 1 included, ratio sets the frame, and labels and locale translate the names, hints and the level. Under reduced motion the zoom steps instantly.

items.name: zoomable-image-demo
items.title: Zoomable image demo
items.description: A working preview of Zoomable image.

items.name: photo-mosaic
items.title: Photo mosaic
items.description: The header gallery of a listing: one large photo, four small ones, and a Show all button on the last, collapsing to one photo on a phone.
items.docs: photos are { src, alt, label }; the first five are shown. total is the number of photos in all, when the gallery holds more than you pass. onOpen(index) is called with the place of the photo that was pressed and onShowAll when the button is, so you open your own lightbox or sheet: the mosaic opens nothing. Every cell is a button named 'Photo 3 of 24: Kitchen'. With fewer than five photos the layout falls back to one, two, three or four. Below about 32rem of its own width it shows the first photo with a '1 / 24' counter (none for a lone photo), and below 48rem the Show all button shrinks to its icon and the count so it never outgrows its cell, its name staying whole. labels and locale translate the names and the number.

items.name: photo-mosaic-demo
items.title: Photo mosaic demo
items.description: A working preview of Photo mosaic.

items.name: justified-gallery
items.title: Justified gallery
items.description: Photos in rows of equal height with no cropping and no gaps, the widths following each photo's own shape, laid out by CSS alone.
items.docs: items are { src, alt, width, height, caption }: the width and height only give the shape. rowHeight is the height the rows aim for (a number in px or any CSS length; the default grows with the window) and gap the space between photos. Every row grows its photos in proportion to their shapes until it fills the width, and the last row keeps its size. On a phone, where a row holds only two or three photos, a very wide photo that does not fit beside the one before it leaves that one alone on a row, stretched to the full width: put such a photo where it fits, or aim for a smaller row. It is flexbox only, with no layout script and no resize observer. With onSelect(index) each photo is a button for your lightbox; without it a photo is a plain figure. Captions appear on hover and, on a button, on focus, and on a touch screen on every photo wide enough to hold one (9rem).

items.name: justified-gallery-demo
items.title: Justified gallery demo
items.description: A working preview of Justified gallery.

items.name: video-facade
items.title: Video facade
items.description: A poster that becomes the player only when pressed, so a page with a video loads no video code and makes no third-party request until it is wanted.
items.docs: Pass provider (youtube, vimeo or file), videoId or src, poster, title and duration. Before the press there is one button with the poster, a play button, the title and the length, and a line under it names the provider that will load; no request is made to YouTube or Vimeo. Pressing swaps in the player (YouTube no-cookie, Vimeo with do-not-track, or a video element), starts it and moves focus into it. onActivate gets the click: call event.preventDefault() to keep the poster while you ask for consent. aspect is the shape of the frame, and a missing or broken poster falls back to a block with the title.

items.name: video-facade-demo
items.title: Video facade demo
items.description: A working preview of Video facade.

items.name: seek-bar
items.title: Seek bar
items.description: The scrubber for any player: played, buffered and remaining, chapters, a time tooltip on hover, and keyboard seeking by seconds.
items.docs: value and duration are in seconds: feed value from timeupdate (or every animation frame for a smoother thumb) and read the visitor's choice from onSeek. buffered is a list of { start, end } ranges, and toBuffered(media.buffered), from @rhs-ui/primitives/seek-bar/time, makes it from a media element. chapters is a list of { start, title } and draws the bar in a piece for each. onSeek fires for every move of a drag, a click and each key press. onSeekStart fires when a drag begins, so you can pause. onSeekEnd fires once on release and after each key press: seek the media only there to keep video from stuttering. The thumb stays where the visitor put it until the player reports that it got there. Keys: arrows seek step seconds (5), Shift three times that, Home and End jump, Page Up and Page Down move a tenth of the length. aria-valuetext reads '1 minute 23 seconds of 4 minutes 56 seconds' (plus the chapter), or whatever valueText returns. A duration of 0, NaN or Infinity turns the bar off: it has no value, and a screen reader hears 'Length not known yet' (or what valueText(0, 0) returns) instead of '0 seconds of 0 seconds'.

items.name: seek-bar-demo
items.title: Seek bar demo
items.description: A working preview of Seek bar.

items.name: volume-control
items.title: Volume control
items.description: A mute button and volume slider that remembers the last level, steps with the arrow keys, says the level in words and folds into a popover when space is short.
items.docs: value is the level from 0 to 1 and muted is a separate flag, so muting keeps the level and unmuting puts it back (from a level of nothing, the last audible one). Control both with onChange and onMutedChange (set media.volume and media.muted there), or leave them to defaultValue and defaultMuted. Moving the slider while muted unmutes. The arrow keys move the level by step (0.05, so 5 percent), Page keys and Shift by half, Home and End go to the ends; on a muted slider a key steps from the level that was muted and unmutes. M mutes and unmutes from the button or the slider. A screen reader hears 'Volume 60 percent' or 'Muted', and the button is named Mute or Unmute. showValue writes the level as a number. With compact the slider stands upright in a popover behind a small button, for a control bar with no room to spare. labels replaces the words.

items.name: volume-control-demo
items.title: Volume control demo
items.description: A working preview of Volume control.

items.name: audio-waveform
items.title: Audio waveform
items.description: A waveform drawn from peak values with a played portion and click-to-seek, as two SVG paths, light enough to repeat fifty times in a list.
items.docs: peaks is a list of numbers from 0 to 1 in time order, as many as you have: the bars are resampled to the width, so one set of peaks fits a list row and a full-width player. progress is how much has played, 0 to 1. barWidth, gap and height are in px. It draws two SVG paths however many bars there are, so fifty in a list is fine. The width is only known in the browser, so on the server a flat dotted line stands in until it has been measured. With interactive it is a slider: a press or drag calls onSeek with a position from 0 to 1, the arrow keys seek 5 seconds (2 percent without a duration), Shift three times that, Home, End and the Page keys jump, and a marker shows where a press will land, with the time when duration is known. A screen reader hears '1 minute 23 seconds of 4 minutes 56 seconds', or '42 percent' without a duration. A still waveform is hidden from assistive technology unless you pass a label. Get peaks from your server, or in the browser with peaksFromArrayBuffer(await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer()), peaksFromAudioBuffer(buffer) or peaksFromChannelData(samples, count), all from @rhs-ui/primitives/audio-waveform/peaks; for a long file work them out once on the server.

items.name: audio-waveform-demo
items.title: Audio waveform demo
items.description: A working preview of Audio waveform.

items.name: media-card
items.title: Media card
items.description: A card for a video, a podcast episode or an image: thumbnail, kind badge, duration chip, title and a progress line, as one link or button.
items.docs: The whole card is one link (pass href) or one button (pass onClick without href), so there is a single tab stop and a single target for a finger. kind is video, audio or image: it sets the icon and the word on the badge (labels={{ audio: 'Podcast' }} says what you show) and the mark in the middle, a play button or a magnifier. thumbnail is decoration (alt is empty) because the title is what is read; without it a calm block stands in. duration is in seconds, drawn bottom right in tabular numbers on a dark chip that holds contrast on any picture, and a screen reader hears it in words. progress from 0 to 1 draws a thin white line in a dark strip along the bottom of the picture, so it reads on a pale picture and on a white page alike, and the card's name then ends with 'Resume at 12:40' (or 'Finished' near the end, when the line is full). Hover only brightens the play mark. aspectRatio is width over height (16 / 9 by default, 1 for cover art): give a grid one ratio and its rows line up. meta is the line under the title, and the title keeps to two lines. labels replaces the words.

items.name: media-card-demo
items.title: Media card demo
items.description: A working preview of Media card.

items.name: file-type-icon
items.title: File type icon
items.description: A file icon picked from the extension or MIME type, drawn in the library's own style, with the extension as a small label.
items.docs: Pass name ('report-final.xlsx'), mime ('application/pdf') or both: the extension in the name wins (it has to look like one, up to eight letters and digits with at least one letter and no spaces, so 'Invoice no. 4821' has none), then the MIME type, then its first part (image/, video/, audio/, text/). You get a page with a folded corner, a glyph and a dark tag with the extension (up to five letters). The families are document, sheet, slide, image, video, audio, archive, code and unknown, and each has a glyph of its own (lines, a grid, a screen, hills, a play mark, a waveform, a zipper, brackets, a question mark), so none is told apart by colour alone. size is sm, md (default) or lg: 28, 40 and 64px wide. sm leaves the tag off, which would be too small to read, and draws the glyph larger; showExtension overrides that either way. FILE_TYPES (extension to family) and MIME_TYPES (MIME type to extension) are plain exported objects: add your own at startup, FILE_TYPES.blend = 'image', and every icon follows. family forces a family, and fileTypeLabel(name, mime) gives 'PDF document' for a label. The icon is hidden from assistive technology unless you pass a label, because the file name beside it carries the meaning. It is a server component: no script is shipped.

items.name: file-type-icon-demo
items.title: File type icon demo
items.description: A working preview of File type icon.

items.name: browser-frame
items.title: Browser frame
items.description: A browser window drawn in CSS around a screenshot or live UI: tab, address bar and window controls, in calm monochrome.
items.docs: Wrap anything in it: a screenshot (an img is made block and full width) or live UI. url is written in the address bar, plain by default or a real link that opens in a new tab with href (the link is the one part of the chrome that stays in the accessibility tree, and says it opens a new tab). title adds a tab; without it the dots and the address share one row, and the address is centred in a field of its own that stands out from the strip in every tone. The chrome is lines and radii only, with three neutral window dots: no images, and no copy of a real browser. It follows the theme tokens, or fix it with tone='light' or tone='dark', for a dark window around a light screenshot whatever the page's theme. The chrome is hidden from assistive technology, and the figure has one caption that says what the window shows: your caption, or a hidden one such as 'Browser window showing Overview, app.northwind.example/overview'. It narrows to 320px without clipping: the address and the tab truncate first. It is a server component, so no script is shipped.

items.name: browser-frame-demo
items.title: Browser frame demo
items.description: A working preview of Browser frame.

items.name: phone-frame
items.title: Phone frame
items.description: A modern phone drawn in CSS around your screenshot or live UI, with island, bezel and side buttons, in the house monochrome.
items.docs: Pass src and alt for a screenshot, or children for live UI. width is the width of the whole device in px or any CSS length (280 by default, never wider than its container), and every size on the device, from the corner radius to the island, is a share of that width in container units, so it scales cleanly from a thumbnail to a life-size 390px. The same units (text-[4.4cqw], p-[5cqw]) are there for the live UI inside it. The screen keeps the 19.5 to 9 shape of a phone and clips its content to the rounded corners. tone is dark (graphite, the default) or light (silver) around a black bezel; notch is island (default) or none. Live UI is padded clear of the island and the home bar (safeArea, on by default) and scrolls inside the screen; turn it off to draw to the edges and use --phone-safe-top and --phone-safe-bottom, which are set on the screen. The body, buttons, island and home bar are hidden from assistive technology, and the screen has the one name: alt for a picture, label (Phone screen) for live UI or a picture without alt. There are no image files. It is a server component.

items.name: phone-frame-demo
items.title: Phone frame demo
items.description: A working preview of Phone frame.

items.name: qr-code
items.title: QR code
items.description: A QR code as crisp SVG from any string, drawn by a bundled encoder with four error correction levels, a quiet zone and SVG and PNG download.
items.docs: value is any string, sent as UTF-8. The encoder is bundled (pure TypeScript, versions 1 to 40, no package and no request): it picks the smallest version that holds the text in the densest mode the text allows, adds Reed-Solomon error correction and keeps the mask a scanner reads most easily. The code is one SVG path, so it is sharp at any size and prints well, and it is always dark modules on a white tile in both themes, because a scanner needs that contrast. size is the width of the tile in px (never wider than its container). level is L, M (default), Q or H: about 7, 15, 25 and 30 percent of the code may be lost, and a higher level is denser. margin is the quiet zone in modules (4, which scanners want). The figure is named after what it leads to, 'QR code for northwind.example/invite', from title or from value without its scheme. With actions a row offers Download SVG (a vector file at least 512px wide, on whole pixels per module, so Figma, Word or Keynote import it at a usable size) and Download PNG; the PNG is drawn from the SVG only when its button is pressed, on whole pixels per module and at least pngSize wide (1024), and onDownload(format, file) is called after either download starts (pass it from a client component). An empty value, or one too long for any code (7089 digits, 4296 capital letters or 2953 bytes at level L), shows a message in place of the tile. encodeQr(value, level) gives the modules for your own drawing and qrSvg(matrix, margin, pixels) a whole SVG document (with pixels it has a width and height). Only the download buttons need a script.

items.title: QR code demo
items.description: A working preview of QR code.

items.name: story-ring
items.title: Story ring
items.description: An avatar with a ring that says whether a story is new, seen or live, as a button that opens it, plus a snapping row with your own slot.
items.docs: StoryRing wraps the house Avatar in a ring with a gap and is one button. state is unseen (a bold solid ring), seen (a thin muted ring), live (a dashed ring with a small Live tag) or none (no ring). The picture keeps its size in all four, so a row stays level, and the ring never depends on colour: weight, dashes and a word carry it. The button is named after the person and their state, 'Maya, new story', 'Maya, story seen', 'Maya, live now', labels replaces those words, and label replaces the whole name. src falls back to the initials of name when it is missing or fails to load. size is sm, md or lg (48, 64 and 80px). onOpen is called when it is pressed. showName writes the name under the ring inside the button, so the two are one target; badge puts a small mark on the bottom right. StoryRingRow is a sideways-scrolling list named Stories that snaps ring by ring: items is a list of { id, name, src, state } and onOpen receives the person. you adds the viewer's own slot first: Your story with a plus when state is none (onAdd), and the ring when they have a story (onOpen). With a mouse, small arrows appear at the ends that can still be scrolled, and smooth scrolling is turned off under reduced motion.

items.title: Story ring demo
items.description: A working preview of Story ring.

items.name: hotspot-image
items.title: Hotspot image
items.description: A picture with numbered markers that open a note, for annotated product shots, floor plans and diagrams. Percent positions, 44px targets, notes that stay on screen.
items.docs: hotspots is a list of { id, x, y, title, body }: x and y are percentages of the picture (0 to 100), so a marker stays on its spot at any width, and the order of the list is the number and the Tab order. Give ratio the shape of your picture (default 3 / 2) so the markers land where you put them. Control the open note with activeId and onActiveChange (null means none), or leave both out; defaultActiveId opens one at load, but a floating note open at load puts a focus guard at each end of the page, so the first Tab lands on an invisible stop. A note floats next to its marker and flips and shifts to stay fully on screen; in a picture narrower than 30rem it opens in a panel under the picture instead, so on a phone it never covers the picture or the page. The markers are white with a dark number in both themes, because a picture does not follow the theme. showList repeats every note as a numbered list under the picture, for screen readers and for phones. Each marker is named '2: Living room'. Tab from an open note moves on to the next marker, Shift+Tab returns to its own, Escape closes. The notes are read-only text; it is not a tour and not a place for comments.

items.name: embed-consent
items.title: Embed consent
items.description: A gate for third-party embeds: it names the provider and what it receives, and loads the iframe only after the visitor agrees, with a way to remember and revoke.
items.docs: Put the provider's iframe in children: it is not rendered, so it makes no request, until the visitor presses Load content. provider names who runs it and is also the key a 'yes, always' is stored under (localStorage under rhs-ui:embed-consent:<provider>, one answer per provider, shared by every embed of it and every tab). remember='always' (default) adds the checkbox; remember='once' stores nothing. receives lists what the provider gets, in short phrases: name what yours really sends. After loading, focus moves to the iframe and a line under it offers Revoke consent (or Hide, when the answer was not remembered); pressing it brings the placeholder back, puts focus on Load content and says 'Content from <provider> hidden.' to a screen reader (labels.hidden). Pass consented, onConsent and onRevoke to let your own consent manager decide instead; the component then stores nothing. The server renders the placeholder, so a returning visitor's embed arrives right after hydration.

items.name: pausable-image
items.title: Pausable image
items.description: An animated GIF or WebP that starts still behind a Play button, so moving images meet the rule for pause, stop and hide. Reduced motion always starts paused.
items.docs: src is the animated file (GIF, animated WebP or APNG, or an animated SVG) and alt is required. Without poster the first frame of src is drawn to a canvas as the still, which loads src up front; with poster nothing animated is requested until Play. The button is one element with aria-pressed, so focus stays on it when it turns from Play into the corner Pause. autoPlay is ignored for a visitor who prefers reduced motion. It is the pause control WCAG 2.2.2 asks for when motion lasts more than five seconds. onPlayingChange reports the state.

items.name: laptop-frame
items.title: Laptop frame
items.description: A laptop drawn in CSS around a screenshot or live UI: lid, bezel, hinge and base, with a lid that opens from 0 to 1 so a scroll position can lift it.
items.docs: Pass src and alt for a screenshot, or children for live UI; the screen keeps 16 / 10 and clips to its corners. Everything on the device is a share of its own width (container units), so it scales with width: set width in px or any CSS length, and size live UI in cqw (text-[1.5cqw]). tone is the body finish, dark (graphite) or light (silver). open (0 to 1) turns the lid on its hinge; feed it a scroll value to lift it on scroll. The device is decoration: the alt of the picture, or label for live UI, is what is read.

items.name: image-tile
items.title: Image tile
items.description: A picture tile with its title on the image, for a category, a destination or a collection: one link, a scrim that keeps the text readable on any photo.
items.docs: The whole tile is one link (href). Give every tile of a grid the same ratio and the rows stay level. align='start' puts the text at the bottom left with the arrow at the right; align='center' centres it over a dim that is deepest behind the text. The text is always white on a scrim, so it reads on any photo in light and dark. Hover pulls the picture in and nudges the arrow, both off under reduced motion; the focus ring is drawn inside the tile. Titles clamp to two lines, and below about 13rem wide the arrow moves to the corner. alt is empty by default because the title names the link. priority loads a tile above the fold at once.

items.title: Image tile demo

items.name: photo-stack
items.title: Photo stack
items.description: A small pile of photos for an album or an attachment set: the cover on top, the rest peeking out at fixed angles, a count chip, and a fan on hover.
items.docs: photos takes up to five { src, alt }, the cover first; count is how many the album holds in all, and the chip shows how many the pile does not. The angles are fixed numbers, so server and browser draw the same pile. fanOnHover opens the pile on hover and keyboard focus; touch screens and reduced motion keep it closed. With href it is a link, with onClick and no href a button, with neither a labelled picture; the name is 'Summer 2025, 24 photos'. On a link or button with a caption the name is read from the caption itself, so what a voice-control user says matches what is on screen. showCaption puts the title and count under the pile; turn it off for the pile alone.

items.title: Photo stack demo
items.description: A working preview of Photo stack.

items.name: pattern-cover
items.title: Pattern cover
items.description: A designed placeholder for missing artwork: a monochrome pattern drawn from any string, the same on server and client, square or round, in theme tokens.
items.docs: seed is any string (a playlist name, a project id): the same seed always draws the same cover. The seed picks one of five families (rings, stripes, a Bauhaus grid, Truchet arcs, a halftone), the layout and whether the cover is light or dark. It is SVG in foreground and muted tokens, with no random numbers, no images and no network. shape is square or round, size a number of px or any CSS length. It is decoration (aria-hidden) unless you give it a label.

items.title: Pattern cover demo
items.description: A working preview of Pattern cover.

items.name: play-clip-button
items.title: Play clip button
items.description: A round button that plays a short sound, such as a pronunciation or a sample, with a progress ring, one clip at a time and no audio loaded until it is pressed.
items.docs: src is the sound and label is the name of the button as a sentence: 'Play pronunciation of cheese'. The audio element is created on the first press, so a page of these loads no audio until one is used. Starting a clip stops any other that is playing, through a shared registry. The button is a toggle with aria-pressed, shows a spinner while the file arrives and 'Could not play' under the button, with a retry arrow, when it cannot; a second press asks for the file again, so a flaky network recovers without a reload. onEnded fires when a clip plays to its end. The ring keeps showing progress under reduced motion and only drops the easing.

items.title: Play clip button demo
items.description: A working preview of Play clip button.

items.name: image-sequence
items.title: Image sequence
items.description: Scrub through a set of frames by dragging or hovering: a 360-degree product spin, a flipbook or a video hover preview, with keyboard stepping and a slider role.
items.docs: frames is a list of image addresses (keep the array stable between renders). mode='drag' turns the picture as the pointer is dragged (sensitivity 1 means dragging across it shows every frame once; loop wraps past the ends); mode='hover' maps the pointer's place along the picture to a frame and rests on the first when it leaves. The first frame shows at once and the rest are preloaded behind it in batches of four, with a thin line along the top; until a frame arrives the nearest loaded one stays up. The picture is a slider named by alt: arrows step one frame, Page Up and Page Down ten percent, Home and End jump, and aria-valuetext reads 'Frame 12 of 36'. autoRotate (drag only) turns it once, slowly, on first view, never under reduced motion. Vertical swipes still scroll the page.

items.name: image-sequence-demo
items.title: Image sequence demo
items.description: A working preview of Image sequence.

items.name: hover-video-preview
items.title: Hover video preview
items.description: A video thumbnail that plays a muted preview after you rest on it, and loads nothing until you do; skipped on touch, Save-Data and reduced motion.
items.docs: poster is the still and previewSrc a short muted clip. Nothing is requested before the pointer or keyboard focus has rested on the tile for delay milliseconds (300): the video element is not even on the page until then, and when you leave it stops and rewinds. The preview is skipped on touch screens, when the browser asks to save data and under reduced motion, where the poster simply stays. The whole tile is one link (href) or one button (onClick), named by its title and length; the video is decoration. duration is seconds or text.

items.name: text-link
items.title: Text link
items.description: The inline link: one underline, one focus ring, and it says when it opens a new tab, downloads a file or marks the page you are on.
items.docs: Use it for links inside running text and short link lists; for a button that navigates, use Button with asChild. tone is underlined (the default: foreground text with a quiet underline that darkens on hover), subtle (muted, underlined only on hover and focus, for footers and link lists) or inherit (takes the colour around it, for banners and alerts, and draws its focus ring in that colour too, so the ring shows on a filled surface). The underline offset and thickness are in em, so they scale with the text, and the focus ring is drawn again on every line when a link wraps. external opens a new tab with rel=noopener, adds a small up-right arrow that stays on the last word and a hidden 'opens in a new tab'. download is true, a file name, or { filename, type, size }: type and size ({ type: 'PDF', size: 2_411_000 }) are shown as 'PDF, 2.4 MB', with the size written out in the locale you pass, and a screen reader hears 'download' before them. current marks the link to the page you are on with aria-current (page by default, or 'step', 'location', 'date', 'time') and a heavier weight. disabled renders a span with role=link and aria-disabled instead of an anchor, so it is never a dead tab stop. hrefLang sets the attribute and adds a hidden 'in German' (the name comes from Intl.DisplayNames). asChild puts the same look on your framework link: pass <Link href> with the text inside as the only child. labels holds the hidden words for another language. textLinkVariants is exported so other components can borrow the look.

items.name: count-tabs
items.title: Count tabs
items.description: Tabs with a count by every label (Open 12, Closed 48): tabular figures, 99+ above a limit, a skeleton while loading, read out as 'Open, 12 items'.
items.docs: tabs is a list of { value, label, count, loading, disabled }. Control the selected tab with value and onValueChange, or leave them out and use defaultValue (the first tab by default); the panels are TabsContent from @rhs-ui/primitives/tabs, passed as children, or leave them out and show one list yourself. variant is line (an underline) or pill (a segmented control). Counts are written in tabular figures in the locale you pass and collapse to '99+' above max (99 by default). The accessible name of a tab is its label and its count, 'Open, 12 items' ('Open, 1 item', 'Shipped, more than 99 items'), so the number is read out with the tab; labels holds those words for another language. loading puts a small skeleton where the number goes and the name says 'loading count'. A tab with a count of zero dims but is not disabled, so the empty view stays reachable (use disabled to switch one off). Arrow keys, Home and End move and select, as in Tabs. When the count of the selected tab changes, one polite announcement says so ('Open, 13 items'); a count that changes in another tab, and the first render, say nothing. A row that is wider than its box scrolls sideways, with room inside the scroller for the focus ring. Without children there are no panels, so the tabs carry no aria-controls.

items.description: A working preview of Count tabs.

items.name: cursor-pagination
items.title: Cursor pagination
items.description: Older and Newer for feeds and APIs that page by cursor: no page numbers, no total, a spinner that keeps the button's width and a plain end state.
items.docs: Pass hasPrevious and hasNext from your API (a cursor, a next-page token, a Link header) and handle onPrevious and onNext; previous is the newer page and next the older one. loading is 'previous', 'next' or false and says which way a request is in flight: that button shows a spinner in place of its arrow, so it keeps its width, and is marked aria-busy, while the other one waits, dimmed. Neither is disabled, so a keyboard user keeps their place and a second press does nothing. When there is nothing further the button is replaced by plain text, 'No newer results' at the start of the list and 'No older results' at the end, instead of a dead control. range is your own text ('21 to 40') in a polite live region, so a screen reader hears where it landed after each step; at an end of the list the same region also says so ('16 to 20. No older results.'). The range is empty until you give it one. When the button that was used with the keyboard (or a click that focused it) is replaced by its end text, focus moves onto the text, so a keyboard user is not thrown out of the list; if the reader has moved on by then, focus is left alone. hrefs ({ previous, next }) makes the buttons real links, for pages a crawler can follow and a reader can open in a new tab; with a handler as well, a plain click goes to the handler and a middle or modified click opens the address. With links and no handlers it can be rendered from a Server Component (a page.tsx): the component is a client component, so only data goes in, and the links are in the HTML. labels holds the four texts for another language. In a container narrower than 24rem the range moves above the two buttons.

items.name: dot-stepper
items.title: Dot stepper
items.description: Page dots for onboarding, carousels and short flows: the current dot stretches into a pill, each dot can be a button, and past seven a window slides.
items.docs: count is how many steps there are and value the current one, counted from 0. Give it onValueChange and every dot becomes a button inside a list (label names the list, 'Steps' by default); each button is named 'Step 3 of 5' and, with labels (one name per dot: ['Welcome', 'Invite your team', ...]), 'Step 2 of 5, Invite your team'; the current one is marked aria-current='step'. Without onValueChange the dots are one picture with a single name, 'Step 2 of 5' (format changes the words; {current} and {total} are the numbers, and a label is added for the current step). The current dot stretches into a pill and the others stay small. Past seven dots the row no longer grows: a window of five slides along as value moves, the dots at its edges shrink to say there is more, and the dots outside the window are hidden and cannot be tabbed to; each button still knows its place in the whole (aria-posinset and aria-setsize). size is sm, md or lg and orientation horizontal or vertical. The dots, and the focus ring, are drawn in currentColor, so a dark photo takes text-white and shows a white ring. As buttons the dots sit 24px apart, so each button is a 24 by 24px target (WCAG 2.5.8); as a picture they sit closer. A dot that is not current is half strength, and the focus ring has room inside the clip. The stretch and the slide are instant under reduced motion. It keeps no state of its own: it is a view of value.

items.title: Dot stepper demo
items.description: A working preview of Dot stepper.

items.name: compact-stepper
items.title: Compact stepper
items.description: A stepper for small spaces: 'Step 2 of 5, Shipping' over a segmented bar, with the full list of steps and their states one tap away.
items.docs: steps is the list of { id, label, description, state, href } and current the index of the step in progress, counted from 0. A step before current is done and one after it is upcoming; set state to 'error' on a step that needs attention. The top line is the counter and the name of the current step ('Step 2 of 5', 'Shipping') in one polite live region, so moving on is announced once; a current step in error also says 'Needs attention' beside its name. Under it a segmented bar has one segment per step: done is a mid grey, the current one is solid and upcoming ones are faint, and the bar is hidden from assistive technology because the text already says it. The All steps button opens a popover, a dialog named 'All steps', with every step, its description and its state in words (Done, Current, Needs attention); the state word sits beside the name and the description has the full width of the row under it. With allowJumpBack, done steps and steps in error before the current one become links in that list when they have an href or you give onStepSelect (a button, or an anchor when the step has an href), and choosing one calls onStepSelect(id, index) and closes the list; upcoming steps and the current one are always plain text. A stepper that is read-only, or whose steps have an href and no onStepSelect, can be rendered from a Server Component; onStepSelect is a function and needs a client parent. A step in error that is not the current one is also named under the bar ('Payment needs attention'). size is md or sm, and labels holds every word for another language. It works in any width, from a 240px column to a full-width header.

items.description: A working preview of Compact stepper.

items.name: adaptive-pagination
items.title: Adaptive pagination
items.description: One pagination that fits its box: numbered pages when there is room, 'Page 3 of 12' with a list of pages and arrows when there is not.
items.docs: page is the current page counted from 1 and pageCount how many there are; onPageChange(page) is called with the page asked for. It measures the width of its own container with a ResizeObserver, never the window, so one component fits a narrow card and a wide table footer. When the container is wide enough it shows first, previous, a window of page numbers with ellipses (siblingCount numbers on each side of the current page, 1 by default, always the same number of slots so the row does not jump), next and last. When it is not, it shows previous, a button that reads 'Page 3 of 12' and opens a grid of every page in a dialog named by its heading, 'Go to page' (arrow keys, Home, End and the Page keys move, it opens on the current page), and next. Until it has been measured the compact layout stands in, because it fits anywhere. The current page carries aria-current='page'. The buttons that go back on the first page and the ones that go on at the last are aria-disabled rather than disabled: they keep focus and a tooltip says why ('You are on the first page'). A change of layout never loses the focused control: previous and next are the same elements in both layouts, and a page number, first or last hands focus to the compact label, previous or next (and the label back to the current page number). hrefFor(page) returns an address and turns every control into a real link for crawlers and new tabs; from a Server Component, which cannot pass a function, give hrefTemplate such as '/orders?page={page}'. With a handler too, a plain click goes to onPageChange and a modified click opens the address. The change is announced politely as 'Page 4 of 12'. align places the row (center by default), locale writes the numbers, and labels holds every word for another language.

items.title: Adaptive pagination demo
items.description: A working preview of Adaptive pagination.

items.name: breadcrumb-siblings
items.title: Breadcrumb with siblings
items.description: A breadcrumb where each level opens a menu of its siblings, so people move sideways without going up first. Long trails fold, long lists filter.
items.docs: items is the trail from the top to the page you are on: { label, href, siblings }. The last item is the current page and is not a link. A crumb with siblings, a list of { label, href } for the pages at its level (itself included), gets a small chevron beside its label: the label stays a link to the crumb's own page and the chevron is a separate button named 'Pages in Projects' ('Pages in {label}'), so both actions work from the keyboard. The menu checks the entry whose href is the crumb's own (aria-current is 'location' for a level above and 'page' for the last crumb), and a list of twelve or fewer opens as a menu. A longer list opens as a dialog instead, named 'Pages in Projects', because a menu may hold only items and not a field: the filter field is in focus, typing filters, Enter follows the first match, Arrow Down moves into the links and Arrow Up from the first one returns to the field, Escape closes, the number of matches is said politely ('5 of 18 pages') and a filter that matches nothing says so. onNavigate(href) takes a plain click on a crumb or a sibling, for a client router; without it the links are followed, and a modified click always opens the address. maxVisible (default 4) is the most crumbs shown: a longer trail keeps the first crumb and the last maxVisible minus one, and the levels in between fold into a menu behind a '...' button right after the first crumb (named 'Show 2 more levels', or 'Show 1 more level'). separator is a slash by default and can be any node. It is built on Breadcrumb, so the nav landmark, the ordered list, the hidden separators and aria-current are the same as the plain one; labels holds the words for another language. The trail stays on one line and measures itself: when it does not fit its box, more levels fold into the same menu, one at a time starting next to the first crumb, until the label of the current page is whole (the first crumb and the current page always stay), and they come back when the box grows. Short of that only the label of the current page gives way, with an ellipsis; the other crumbs keep their labels, up to a maximum width, and the gaps tighten on a phone.

items.name: nav-rail
items.title: Nav rail
items.description: A slim vertical rail of icon destinations with tooltips, badges, a top slot and a pinned bottom group, for apps with many areas.
items.docs: items is the list of areas: { id, label, icon, href, badge, badgeLabel, group }. icon is an element (<IconHome />), label is the tooltip, the label under the icon and the accessible name, and an area with an href is a link while one without is a button. current is the id of the area you are in: it is filled and marked aria-current='page'. onSelect(id) is called when one is chosen; on an area with an href a plain click goes to it and a modified click opens the address. badge is a number (the NotificationBadge count: hidden at 0, '99+' above 99) or true for a dot, and badgeLabel (default 'updates') says what it stands for, so a screen reader hears 'Messages 3 unread messages' for a count and 'Reports New report' for a dot: the label comes first in the markup and is drawn after the icon. Entries that follow each other with the same group sit together, and a thin rule is drawn where the group changes. top holds the brand mark; bottom is pinned under the list, for settings and the account, and NavRailItem (label, icon, href, current, onSelect) makes entries there that match the rest. The list is a plain ul inside a nav landmark (label, 'Main' by default), so Tab walks it. On a short screen the list scrolls on its own and top and bottom stay in place, with room inside the scroller for the focus ring. showLabels widens the rail and puts each name under its icon, so the tooltips are not needed. expandOnHover keeps the rail's width and slides a labelled panel over the content when the pointer is over it or focus is inside it, so nothing shifts; expanded holds that panel open. Reduced motion shows it without the slide.

items.name: top-bar
items.title: Top bar
items.description: The app bar of a phone-first screen: a back button, a title that truncates properly, trailing actions and a large title that settles on scroll.
items.docs: Put the bar inside the element that scrolls, as its first child: with sticky (the default) it stays at the top, and the nearest scrolling parent is found by itself (scrollContainer takes a ref when it is another element). title is the name of the screen and subtitle a lighter line under it. onBack shows a back button, a chevron named by backLabel ('Back to orders'; 'Back' by default), and backHref makes it a link that onBack still handles on a plain click; leading replaces it with your own element. actions is a list of { id, label, icon, onSelect, href, disabled, destructive, priority, pinned } shown as icon buttons named by their label. The bar measures itself: when the back button, the whole title and the actions no longer fit, the actions fold into a 'More actions' menu before the title is cut, the lowest priority first (equal priorities from the end), pinned ones never; only when even the menu button leaves too little room does the title truncate with an ellipsis, and its full text stays in the page for assistive technology. large adds a big title under the bar that scrolls away with the content; as it goes under the bar the bar's own title fades in, the progress being read from where the big title is, not from a number you pass. The title is always the one heading: the large one when there is one (the bar's copy is then hidden from assistive technology) and the bar's own otherwise, so the outline never doubles; as sets its level, h1 by default, so pass h2 or lower on a page that has its own h1. The bar adds the top safe-area inset (env(safe-area-inset-top), or the CSS variable --top-bar-inset when that is larger, for a frame that draws its own notch). A sticky bar has a bottom border only once content has scrolled under it (once the large title has gone, when there is one); a bar that is not sticky always has one; borderless removes it. labels holds the two hidden names for another language.

items.name: floating-player
items.title: Floating player
items.description: Keeps a playing video in view: when it scrolls away it docks to a corner as a mini player that never restarts, with a close button.
items.docs: Wrap any player in it (a video element, an iframe or your own component) and tell it whether the media is playing with playing. While the player is on screen nothing changes. When it scrolls out of view during playback, the same element docks to a corner as a mini player (dock is bottom-right by default or bottom-left, width is a number of px or any CSS length, 320 by default, never wider than the screen minus 2rem): the child is not moved or re-created, only restyled with position fixed, so playback never restarts, and a placeholder of the same height, with a dashed outline and a short note, keeps the page from jumping and shows where it went. It counts as in view while about a fifth of it is on screen. A video that is not playing is never docked; once docked, pausing keeps the mini player so it can be resumed. The mini player is a labelled region ('Product tour, mini player', from label) with a Close button and a 'Back to video' link that scrolls to the placeholder; Escape closes it from inside it and from anywhere nothing else has focus (a menu or dialog that takes the key keeps it), and docking is announced once. Closing calls onClose, where you pause the media, and the player stays in its place until the video has been seen again; onDock(true | false) tells you when it docks and when it returns. Focus goes to the player when the mini player closes or you go back. It keeps clear of a phone's safe area (env(safe-area-inset-*), at least 1rem from each edge), and under reduced motion it docks without the slide. Do not put it inside an element with a transform, filter or contain: paint, which would make fixed mean fixed inside that element. The scroll can be the page's or any scroll container's. labels holds the words for another language. The rhs-float-in keyframes and its animate-rhs-float-in variable come with the item.

items.name: alphabet-index
items.title: Alphabet index
items.description: An A to Z rail to jump through a long list: drag a finger down it, see the letter in a bubble, skip the empty letters.
items.docs: Put it beside a scrolling list and give it a height (h-full inside a flex row). Pass letters as a string or an array (years and numbers work), available for the letters that have entries, value for the one your list is showing, and scroll the list to that section in onSelect. Press or drag along the rail with a finger, a pen or a mouse: onSelect is called once per letter crossed, the bubble shows it, and letters without entries give way to the nearest one that has some. For the keyboard it is a list of buttons: Tab enters it at the current letter, the arrow keys, Home and End move, Enter selects, and Tab or Shift+Tab leaves it from wherever focus is. Set bubble to false to leave the bubble out.

items.name: route-focus
items.title: Route focus
items.description: After a client-side navigation it moves focus to the new page's heading and announces the title once, as the browser does for full loads.
items.docs: Mount it once in the root layout and pass the pathname from your router (usePathname() in Next.js). When the path changes it moves focus to the page's main heading, or to the element you name with target (a selector or a ref), and says the page title once in a polite live region. The first render, a change of hash or query string, and a navigation while the person is typing in a field do nothing to focus. The target gets a temporary tabindex of -1 and shows no outline unless focus arrived by keyboard. Pass resetScroll if your router does not scroll to the top by itself.

items.name: stage-path
items.title: Stage path
items.description: A chevron path through stages (Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Won): done, current and next, clickable when you allow it.
items.docs: Pass stages (id, label, optional date and note) and current, the id of the stage the item is at. Without onStageChange it is a read-only record. With it, every stage you may go to is a button that calls onStageChange(id, from) before anything moves: change current yourself when you accept, and return a promise to have the stage shown as busy meanwhile. Going back to a finished stage needs allowBackward. lostLabel adds a terminal outcome (it calls onStageChange with the id "lost"), and lost draws the item as ended there, with current as the last stage it reached. When a press made with the keyboard or a pointer moves the item, focus follows it to the stage it is at (or the outcome), which is no longer a button, so the keyboard keeps its place; the arrow keys pass through that stage and Tab still goes from button to button. A screen reader hears an ordered list (Stage 3 of 5: Proposal, current) and, politely, what happened (Proposal, stage 3 of 5, or Closed lost at stage 3 of 5; every sentence can be reworded through labels); in a box under 28rem only the current stage keeps its name and the others shrink to a check or a number.

items.name: category-strip
items.title: Category strip
items.description: A scrolling row of icon-and-label categories with the current one underlined, for browsing marketplaces and stays.
items.docs: Pass categories (id, label, icon, href, count) and current. Without an href an item is a button marked aria-pressed and onSelect(id) is called; with one it is a link marked aria-current="page", drawn by linkAs (your router Link), and onSelect, if given, takes the plain click over so you can route yourself. The row scrolls sideways behind fade edges with arrows that appear only where more is hidden, a mouse can drag it and it glides on, touch keeps its momentum, and the arrow keys, Home and End move between the items with one tab stop for the whole strip. When the row first appears with the current category inside a fade, it is centred (and kept centred while a web font widens the labels, until you scroll, press a key or focus an item), and it scrolls into view when it changes. Labels are never cut: a label sets the width of its item. size is sm, md or lg. Without panels: choosing a category only changes what your page shows below.

items.name: lazy-tabs
items.title: Lazy tabs
items.description: Tabs whose panels load when first opened, with a skeleton, an error and Retry per panel, and the loaded ones kept.
items.docs: Give each tab a load: a function that returns a promise of the panel content, run the first time the tab opens, or plain content for a tab that needs no request. A panel shows the skeleton you pass (per tab or for all), then the content, which is kept so coming back is instant. If the promise rejects the panel says Could not load <tab> with a Retry button (an Error message is shown under it), and no other panel is touched. prefetchOnHover starts a tab after the pointer rests on it for a moment, or at once on focus. A loading tab swaps its icon for a spinner in the same box (a tab without an icon pulses its label), so no tab ever moves while another loads, and its panel is aria-busy; a request is never cancelled by leaving the tab. A row wider than its box scrolls sideways behind fade edges with the selected tab kept in view. keepMounted keeps loaded panels mounted (hidden) so their state survives. Panels are drawn from tabs, so there are no TabsContent children.

items.title: Lazy tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Lazy tabs.

items.name: closable-tabs
items.title: Closable tabs
items.description: Tabs you can close and add: a close button on each tab, a plus at the end, and a sensible tab chosen after closing.
items.docs: Pass tabs (id, label, icon, closable, dirty), value and onValueChange, and render TabsContent panels as children. Each tab has a close button named Close <label>; a middle click or Delete on a tab asks for it to close as well. onClose(id) is only a request: nothing closes until you remove the tab from tabs, so you can show a confirmation first. When the selected tab goes, the nearest neighbour (to its right, else to its left) is selected through onValueChange and takes focus. A dirty tab shows a dot instead of the close button until hover or focus and says unsaved changes in its name. onAdd adds the plus button; at maxTabs it stays focusable, dimmed, and explains why. A tab with closable false is pinned: it has no close button, and a small pin stands where the button would be so every tab keeps the same room. Overflow scrolls behind fade edges with the selected tab kept in view; the arrows appear where there is a hover, and touch swipes. If you confirm in a dialog, focus is put on the neighbour tab after the dialog has closed; when the person keeps the tab, return focus to it in the dialog's onCloseAutoFocus.

items.name: archive-nav
items.title: Archive nav
items.description: A blog or changelog archive by year and month, with post counts, the current period open and the rest folded.
items.docs: Pass periods (year and months, each with month 1 to 12, count and href), current ({ year, month }) and your application locale. The current year is open and the others are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded; a month is a link (drawn by linkAs, your router Link) only if it has posts, and the current one is marked aria-current="page". Without an href, a month is a button that calls onNavigate. Month names are worked out from the locale. The newest collapsedCount years (default 5) show and the rest sit behind a Show earlier years button that never moves, so keyboard focus stays on it; if the current page is in an older year they start shown. The list is one nav landmark, named Archive by default.

items.name: load-earlier
items.title: Load earlier
items.description: Load earlier messages at the top of a feed without the scroll jumping: it keeps your place when older items arrive.
items.docs: Put it first in the scrolling list, above the items, and pass hasEarlier, loading, error and onLoadEarlier. When the older items are added above, the row keeps the reader on the item they were looking at: it measures that item before and after and corrects the scroll position by the difference, so it works where the browser does not anchor the scroll and does not correct twice where it does. Pass scrollRef when the list scrolls inside a box (otherwise the nearest scrolling ancestor, or the page, is used). Set auto to load when the row scrolls into view; the button stays as the fallback. Pass count and noun to have what arrived announced once as a count (12 earlier messages loaded). Keep the list itself out of a live region, or every old message would be read out. The row has four states: the button, a spinner row, an error with Retry, and a quiet start of the conversation.

items.name: accessible-feed
items.title: Accessible feed
items.description: An infinite feed built to the WAI-ARIA feed pattern: each article is a stop, and Page Down and Page Up move between them.
items.docs: Pass items, renderItem (what is inside an article), labelFor (the name of an article), hasMore, loading and onLoadMore. The container is role=feed and aria-busy while loading; every item is an article and a tab stop with aria-posinset, aria-setsize (-1 while the total is unknown, or the total you pass) and aria-label. Page Down and Page Up move focus to the next and previous article; Page Down on the last one asks for more and moves on when it arrives; Ctrl+End and Ctrl+Home leave the feed for the next or previous focusable element. New items never take focus. Under the feed it renders InfiniteScrollStatus: loading by itself near the viewport, a visible Load more button, an error with Retry and the end; pass status for its words, noun and margin. articleClassName styles each article; the look inside is yours.
