items.name: swipe-tabs
items.title: Swipe tabs
items.description: Tabs for phones: panels swipe sideways on scroll-snap, the underline follows your finger between tabs, and a mouse gets plain tabs with arrow keys.
items.docs: Give it a height when the panels should scroll on their own (h-full inside a flex column, or a fixed height); without one it is as tall as its tallest panel. Pass tabs (value, label, icon, content), then value and onValueChange to control it, or defaultValue. The panels are one row of scroll-snap, so the browser does the swiping and the momentum: a swipe selects the new tab once the track has settled, a tap on a tab slides to its panel, and the underline and the label colours are drawn from the scroll position on every frame. Only the selected panel is exposed to assistive technology; the others are inert. lazy mounts the selected panel and its neighbours only, and a tap on a far tab starts one panel away so the slide never shows a blank. swipeable={false} leaves the tabs and the arrow keys (Left, Right, Home, End) as the only way to move. Under reduced motion the slide is an instant change. A bar of tabs wider than the screen scrolls with the underline, keeps the selected tab in view and fades at the edge it continues past. It follows right-to-left text. A controlled parent that refuses a change gets the track slid back to the selected tab. Use barClassName for a sticky bar and panelClassName for the padding of the panels.

items.name: floating-tab-bar
items.title: Floating tab bar
items.description: A floating, pill-shaped tab bar for mobile web: only the current tab shows its label, five fit in 320px, and it clears the home indicator.
items.docs: Pass items (id, label, icon, href, badge), current and onSelect. Only the current item shows its label, with an animated width that is instant under reduced motion; the other items are icons that keep their label as the accessible name, so three to five destinations fit on a phone. badge is a count or true for a dot, from NotificationBadge. The bar is fixed to the bottom and pads for the safe area (the page needs viewport-fit=cover in its viewport meta for the inset to have a value); to pin it inside a frame instead, pass className="absolute" to a positioned parent. hideOnScroll slides it away while the page scrolls down and brings it back on any upward move, at the top of the page, and when a key brings focus into it; scrollRef names an element that scrolls instead of the page, and it must exist before the bar. With linkAs it renders in a Server Component (only the scroll behaviour is client code); onSelect is a function, so use it from a Client Component.

items.name: expanding-search
items.title: Expanding search
items.description: A header search icon that grows into a field in place, with suggestions, Escape to fold back and a full-bar cover on phones.
items.docs: Put it in the end of a header; the header should be position: relative, because on a phone the field covers it. Control the text with value and onValueChange (or defaultValue), handle Enter with onSubmit, and pass suggestions (strings or { value, hint }) that you have filtered yourself: they appear under the field while it has focus, with arrow keys, Enter and the typed part in bold, and a click on a row calls onSubmit with it. expandedWidth sets how wide the field grows on a screen wider than a phone (a number of px or a CSS length), align="start" grows it towards the end instead. listOpen shows the suggestions whatever has focus, for a preview or your own logic. shortcut opens it from anywhere outside other fields: "/" or "mod+k". Escape and the close button fold it back and return focus to the icon; leaving an empty field folds it too, and one with text stays open so a query is never thrown away. A folded field keeps its text and shows a dot on the icon. The button is named Search and reports aria-expanded. Pass open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange to control it, and autoFocus to focus a field that mounts open.

items.name: toc-rail
items.title: Contents rail
items.description: A quiet contents rail for long articles: one mark per heading in the page gutter, opening into the titles on hover, focus or a touch button.
items.docs: Put it in a column of the page next to the article, in the outer gutter, and leave about 16rem free there: the rail is 2.5rem wide at rest and grows over the gutter, never over the text. Pass items (id, title, level 1 to 3) in page order; the ids are the ids of the headings. It follows the scroll by itself, or takes activeId. offset is the room, in px, a fixed header takes: the rail sticks that far from the top and a heading counts as reached when it passes that line (give the headings scroll-margin-top to match). side="left" mirrors it. It is a nav with a list of links and aria-current="location": a mouse opens it by pointing, the keyboard by Tab, and a small button, drawn only where the pointer is a finger, holds it open (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange). Below the lg breakpoint it is hidden: put a contents control at the top of the article for phones.

items.name: story-progress
items.title: Story progress
items.description: Segmented progress bars for stories and slideshows: tap the thirds to move, hold to pause, nothing advances under reduced motion.
items.docs: It wraps the media area: pass count, the slide you are on as index with onIndexChange (or defaultIndex), and put the current slide in children, leaving about 3rem free at the top for the segments and the buttons. duration is a number of ms or one per slide; onComplete is called when the last slide's time is up and when someone goes forward from it; going back from the first slide restarts it. A press on the left third goes back and on the right third goes on; holding anywhere pauses while it is down. Links, buttons and fields inside the slide keep working. Keyboard users get Left and Right on the story, a Pause button, and Previous and Next buttons that appear on focus; "Slide 2 of 5" is said once in a polite live region. paused and onPausedChange control the Pause button, autoplay={false} stops the timer so the current segment is simply full, and a hidden tab pauses by itself. The fill is a CSS animation, so pausing keeps the exact place, and under reduced motion nothing advances on its own and the Pause button is not drawn. tone="media" draws white segments for a photo or a dark slide; actions adds buttons beside Pause.

items.name: card-tabs
items.title: Card tabs
items.description: Tabs whose triggers are cards with an icon, a title and a line, for choosing between jobs, plans or modes, with real tabpanels and 2D arrow keys.
items.docs: Pass tabs (value, title, description, icon, count, disabled), value and onValueChange (or defaultValue), and CardTabsContent panels as children, one per value. orientation="horizontal" is a grid of columns cards per row from the sm breakpoint (default the number of tabs, at most 3) and a single column on a phone; "vertical" is a list beside the panel from md up. The selected card has a stronger border and an inverted icon tile, which read without colour. They are real tabs, and a card is named by what it shows (title, count and line), so what someone sees is what a voice command or a screen reader says; arrow keys move and select, and Up and Down also move by a whole row, measured from the layout as it is right now, so a phone's single column steps one card at a time. icon is an element, so pass <IconRocket />. The count is written with locale. The selected panel is a tab stop, so it shows a focus ring when the keyboard reaches it.

items.name: responsive-dialog
items.title: Responsive dialog
items.description: One dialog API that is a centred modal on desktop and a bottom drawer on phones, switching live without losing the content's state.
items.docs: Pass title and description (both required, and both wired into either shape), a trigger, the children and an optional footer, then open and onOpenChange to control it or leave them out. It is one element that changes shape, not two components: above breakpoint (640px by default) it is a centred dialog, below it a bottom drawer with a grab handle that closes on a drag past a third of its height or a quick flick; resize or rotate while it is open and nothing in the children is remounted, so typed text and scroll positions stay. Tall children scroll in the body while the title and the footer stay; the footer pads for the home indicator in the drawer (the page needs viewport-fit=cover in its viewport meta for that inset to have a value). Focus lands on a child marked data-autofocus, else on the first field, else on the title, and returns to the trigger on close. dismissible={false} turns off Escape, an outside tap, the close button and the drag, so only your own buttons close it. The viewport is read after mount, so server and browser markup agree.

items.name: choice-dialog
items.title: Choice dialog
items.description: A dialog for choosing between outcomes, not just yes or no: radio options with a line of consequence each, the safest preselected, and a confirm that names the choice.
items.docs: Pass title, description, options (id, label, description, destructive) and onConfirm(id, { remember }), plus a trigger, or open and onOpenChange to control it. The options are a radio group: arrow keys move, and Enter confirms. The first option that is not destructive is selected when it opens, so the safe answer is already chosen; defaultValue picks another. A destructive option takes the destructive style only while it is selected, and the confirm button follows it. confirmLabel is a string or a function of the chosen option, so the button reads "Delete all events"; without it the button repeats the option's label. rememberLabel adds a checkbox whose state is passed to onConfirm. Return a promise from onConfirm: while it is pending the whole dialog is locked, Escape and outside clicks included, and the button shows a spinner; when it resolves the dialog closes, and when it rejects the error message shows inside the dialog, which stays open for another try, and focus returns to the control that was pressed. The panel is never taller than the screen: the title and the buttons stay in view and the options scroll between them, so on a phone held sideways Confirm is still in reach. Nothing chosen last time is carried into the next opening.
